newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's upgrades Tokuyama long-term debt to Baa3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's upgrades Tokuyama long-term debt to Baa3.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it had upgraded its rating of Tokuyama Corp's long-term debt to Baa3 from Ba1.

Moody's said the upgrade reflected its expectations of a good operating performance at Tokuyama, allowing the company to maintain solid debt protection measures in the medium term despite Japan's generally difficult business climate.

The rating agency said it believes Tokuyama's leading world market position in polycrystalline silicon, its successful niche strategy for chemical products, and diversity of operations will increase its long-term business potential.

The debt securities affected are Tokuyama's 20 billion yen 2.2 percent convertible bonds due 2003, 10 billion yen 2.75 percent straight bonds due 2002, 10 billion yen 2.90 percent straight bonds due 2003, 10 billion yen 2.75 percent straight bonds due 2001 and 20 billion yen Japanese shelf due 1998, Moody's said.
